claim: The grid cell network in the medial entorhinal cortex (MEC) has been subject to thorough testing and analysis.
source: The grid cell network in the medial entorhinal cortex (MEC) has been subject to thorough testing and analysis, and many theories for their formation have been suggested.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of research in the field, drawing from established scientific knowledge.

claim: Many theories for grid cell formation have been suggested.

claim: The study re-analyzed data from Bonnevie et al., 2013, in which the hippocampus was inactivated and grid cells were recorded in the rat MEC.

evidence: This statement references the source of the data and the experimental design from a cited study.

claim: The study investigated whether the firing associations of grid cells depend on hippocampal inputs.
source: We investigated whether the firing associations of grid cells depend on hippocampal inputs.
evidence: This describes the research question of the current study.

claim: The study examined temporal and spatial correlations in the firing times of simultaneously recorded grid cells before and during hippocampal inactivation.
source: Specifically, we examined temporal and spatial correlations in the firing times of simultaneously recorded grid cells before and during hippocampal inactivation.
evidence: This describes the specific analytical approach used in the study.

claim: The analysis revealed evidence of network coherence in grid cells even in the absence of hippocampal input to the MEC.
source: Our analysis revealed evidence of network coherence in grid cells even in the absence of hippocampal input to the MEC, both in regular grid cells and in those that became head-direction cells after hippocampal inactivation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on the data analysis performed.

claim: Network coherence was observed both in regular grid cells and in those that became head-direction cells after hippocampal inactivation.

claim: The findings favor models which suggest that phase relations between grid cells in the MEC are dependent on intrinsic connectivity within the MEC.
source: This favors models, which suggest that phase relations between grid cells in the MEC are dependent on intrinsic connectivity within the MEC.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the context of existing theoretical models.

claim: The mechanism responsible for the emergence of grid cell periodicity is arguably one of the best-tested and best-established mechanisms across neural circuits in the mammalian central nervous system.
source: The mechanism responsible for the emergence of grid cell periodicity is arguably one of the best-tested and best-established mechanisms, across neural circuits in the mammalian central nervous system, thanks to extensive testing and analysis (Hafting et al., 2005; Moser et al., 2008; Derdikman and Knierim, 2014; Rowland et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Modeling work has suggested that grid cells are generated intrinsically in the medial entorhinal cortex (MEC), for example by a continuous attractor network model.

evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to modeling studies.

claim: Modeling work has suggested that grid cells have their properties form through an interaction with another region, such as the hippocampus.
